The Bank and Its Subsidiaries’ Overview Performance 
The Bank and Its Subsidiaries’ Performance for Year of 2021 
In 2021, Thailand faced the challenges from continuing new wave of Delta variant  of COVID-19 pandemic 
during second and third quarters. Thus, government declared the series of tighten containment measures in order to 
limit the spread. Thereafter the daily COVID-19 cases gradually declined as well as the accelerated vaccination rollout 
to mitigate highly transmissible COVID -19 variants, the partially relaxation of  COVID-19 containment measures and 
the reopening plan for tourism were implemented in September and  1st November respectively. As a result, domestic 
demand began to show signs of recovery in the fourth quarter of 2021 . However, the firms  have experienced an 
uneven recovery across sectors from the worsening scar left by the previous wave of COVID-19 pandemic (K-shaped 
recovery). Consequently,  the Bank emphasized the prudent banking business especially on a close monitoring of 
asset quality management together with a gradual increase of coverage ratio given thorough considerations on 
various factors with high uncertainties. The Bank continuously provided assistant to the affected customers for both 
retail and business  through 7 financial measures including instant short - term measures, specific  to customers 
measures and long -term debt restructuring measure  to support and alleviate the affected customers during their 
difficult times. The Bank played a key role to support the Covid-19 containment projects. 
The Bank also develop technology and financial disbursement and payment structure as a key part to   
support the government stimulus schemes ie “Thai Chana” Platform, “Mor33 Rao Rak Kan” (financial relief package 
given to private employees covered by Section 33 of the Social Security Act), “Khon La Khrueng” ( Let’s Go Halves 
scheme), “Rao Tiew Duay Kan” (We Travel Together), "Ying Chai Ying Dai" (The More You Spend, The More You Get 
scheme to improve the living standard of people. In addition, on December 1, 2021, Fitch Ratings has upgraded the 
Bank’s rating by one notch on both Foreign Currency Long-Term Rating to BBB+ and National Long-Term Rating to 
AAA (tha). The rating actions reflect KTB's resilience and prominent role to support government policy and its scheme 
over the course of the COVID-19 related economic challenges in Thailand. 
 The Bank and its subsidiaries’ net profit attributable to equity holders of the Bank amounted Baht 21,588 million, 
increased by 29.0% YoY, driven by strong loan growth of 12.6% Ytd. Coverage ratio increased to 168.8% from 147.3% 
as at December 31, 2020 ratio given thorough considerations on various factors with high uncertainties. While being 
able to manage and continuously control asset quality,hence NPLs Ratio-Gross decreased to 3.50 % from 3.81% as at 
December 31, 2020. The expected credit losses has been set aside at the high level of Baht 32,524 million, however, 
decreased by 27.6% YoY.

 The consolidated pre-provision profit before expected credit losses and income tax expenses in 2021 was Baht  
63,055 million, a decrease of 8.3%YoY. The compression was attributable to the interest income from loan in relation to 
partial payment from the auction of mortgaged guarantee assets of Y2020. If excluding interest income received from 
the auction, pre-provision profit declined by 1.5% YoY in response to the low interest rate environment, hence NIM stood 
at 2.49%. Other operating expenses has been managed to decrease by 1.4%. This resulted in cost to income ratio of 
45.5%, a similar level to cost to income ratio if excluding special transactions in 2020. 
The Bank’s Tier 1 and Total Capital ratios were 16.54% and 19.88% respectively, maintaining at a strong level 
as compared to BOT’s requirement.

The Bank and Its Subsidiaries’ Performance for 4Q2021 
Comparing 4Q2021 to the same period of last year, the Bank and its subsidiaries ’ consolidated net profit 
attributable to equity holders of the Bank amounted Baht 4,944 million, increased by 43.2% YoY. This was mainly 
derived from total operating income expansion due to an increase in net interest income of 5.0% as the strong growth 
of quality loans, NIM stood at 2.47%, together with an increase in total other operating income . Other operating 
expenses increased by 5.6% from impairment loss of properties for sale.The Bank and its subsidiaries had set aside 
the expected credit losses of Baht 8,233 million, decreased by 11.0%, however, led to higher coverage ratio.  
 Compared to 3Q2021, KTB’s consolidated total operating income expanded 5.6% from non-interest income 
together with an increase in net interest income of 1.0%, though other operating expenses increased 12.4% due to 
impairment loss of properties for sale, an increase in IT cost to support its digital st rategy together with an increase 
in marketing activities and employee expenses as seasonality .Consequently, pre-provision profit before expected 
credit losses and income tax expenses decreased by 0.2%, result to the decline of  net profit attributable to eq uity 
holders of the Bank of 2.2% QoQ. The expected credit losses were set aside in the similar level to previous quarter 
given thorough considerations on various factors with high uncertainties . 
 The Bank and its subsidiaries had incorpora ted Infinitas By Krungthai Co ., Ltd. as a R&D hub for newly 
digitized financial products, becoming a service provider for various Innovation & Digital Platform, moving 
toward Open Banking, Virtual Digital Banking Service and new business model opportunitie s as well as 
strengthening mega platform such as Pao Tang Application as the country ’s digital infrastructure. In addition, 
the Bank and its subsidiaries  had entered into a joint venture arrangement with Accenture Solutions Co .,Ltd and 
incorporated Arise by Infinitas Co., Ltd. to provide a wold-class human resource service on technology to support the 
digital business growth in Thailand and other countries.

 In 2021, KTB’s consolidated pre-provision profit was Baht 63,055 million, declined by 8.3% YoY, depsite of a 
12.6% loan growth Ytd. The compression was attributable to interest income from loan in relation to partial payment from 
the auction of mortgaged guarantee assets of Y2020 . If excluding interest income received from the auction , pre-
provision profit declined by 1.5% YoY in response to the low interest rate environment. The Bank and its subsidiaries 
had set aside the allowance for expected credit losses decreased by 27.6% YoY.  Hence, consolidated net profit 
attributable to equity holders of the Bank was Baht 21,588 million, an increase by 29.0% YoY. 
 In 4Q2021, KTB’s consolidated pre-provision profit was Baht 15,214 million, an increase of 4.0% YoY. This was 
the result of an increase in total operating income from both net interest income of 5.0% as the focusing on growth of 
quality loan together with an expanded other operating income, whilst the increase in total operating expenses of5.6%.  
Such increase of total operating expenses was mainly due to impairment loss of properties for sale. The Bank and its 
subsidiaries had set aside the expected credit losses amounted Baht 8,233 million, a decrease by 11.0% YoY; hence, 
consolidated net profit attributable to equity holders of the Bank amounted to Baht 4,944 million, increased by 43.2% 
YoY.

 In 2020, given the assessment on Thai economy’s contraction from impact of global pandemic, the Monetary 
Policy Committee, Bank of Thailand had an nounced series of policy rate cuts, having 3 times cut to 0.50%. in May 
2020. Furthermore, the Bank of Thailand announced the measure on lower contribution from financial institutions to 
the FIDF (FIDF fee) from 0.46% to 0.23% as announced on April 7, 2020. The Bank had gradually been cutting lending 
rates of MLR, MOR and MRR until the latest cut in May 2020 to help business operators and retail customers. BOT has 
recently extended the lowered FIDF fee until ended 2022.

In 2021, the Bank and its subsidiaries ’ expected credit losses amounted Baht  32,524 million, decreasing 
27.6% YoY given thorough considerations of various factors in the continuously changing business environment and in this 
economic situation of high uncertainties.  The Bank’s consolidated coverage ratio increased to 168.8% from 163.9 % 
as at September 30, 2021 and from 147.3% as at December 31, 2020, though having an improvement in NPL ratio. 
In 4Q2021, the Bank and its subsidiaries  thoroughly considered various factors in the continuously changing 
business environment and in this economic situation of high uncertainties that could impact loan quality; hence, the  
expected credit losses amounted Baht  8,233 million, decreasing 11.0% YoY. Compared to 3Q2021, the expected 
credit losses were set aside in the similar level to previous quarter.

(2020) with measure on loan payment holiday ending October 22, 2020, BOT had additionally announced on October

financial institution to SME during this uncertain situation of the pandemic .  Guideline included: 
1. To consider debt restructuring  for SME based on their repayment capability .   In the case of financial 
institution undergoes debtor’s evaluation process on debt restructuring, it is allowed for financial institution 
to maintain debtor’s asset classification till December 31, 2020 as prior to pre-relief measure.

financial institution to provide assistance in the form of payment holiday on principal and/ or interest based

month in conjunction with extending the qualification of eligible soft loan  borrower to include company in MAI.

Relief Measures in 2021 
On March 23, 2021, The Bank of Thailand, the Ministry of Finance, and related parties recognized a number 
of challenges from the COVID-19 pandemic faced to the Thai economy since early 2020. Moreover, the business 
recovery is likely to be uneven, especially for SMEs with limited access to capital, as well as businesses that are 
hard-hit by the pandemic . Under such circumstances, the existing short -term relief measure is insufficient t o 
handle the prolonged nature of the situation. BOT and the Ministry of Finance, then, proposed two new measures 
include 1) Soft loan facility for businesses (totaling 250 billion baht) to support viable small and medium enterprises 
(SMEs) affected by the COVID-19 crisis and 2) Debt restructuring through Asset Warehousing with Buy -Back 
options ( totaling 100 billion baht ) provides standardized debt restructuring program for adversely affected 
borrowers whose businesses require prolonged recovery period, whil e possessing viable business models and 
collaterals. The details are as follows
